hints: Focus on converting each quantity into moles, since moles tell you directly how many particles you have.
Remember that for a gas, moles = volume / 24, and for a solid or liquid sample, moles = mass / Mr. Try calculating the moles for argon first.
For the same 6.0 g mass, the substance with the smallest Mr gives the most moles, so compare the Mr values of CO2, Mg and H2O.
walkthrough:
**Recall the key idea**

More moles means more particles. So our job is simply to find which option has the largest number of moles.

Remember the two rules:
$$n = \frac{V}{24} \text{ for gases at room conditions (}V\text{ in dm}^3\text{) }$$
$$n = \frac{m}{M_r} \text{ for masses (}m\text{ in g) }$$

**Calculate moles for option A**

Argon is a gas, so use volume.
$$n(\text{Ar}) = \frac{6.0}{24} = 0.25 \text{ mol}$$

**Calculate moles for options B, C and D**

Now use mass divided by Mr.
$$M_r(\text{CO}_2) = 12.0 + (2 \times 16.0) = 44.0$$
$$n(\text{CO}_2) = \frac{6.0}{44.0} = 0.136 \text{ mol}$$

$$A_r(\text{Mg}) = 24.3$$
$$n(\text{Mg}) = \frac{6.0}{24.3} = 0.247 \text{ mol}$$

$$M_r(\text{H}_2\text{O}) = (2 \times 1.0) + 16.0 = 18.0$$
$$n(\text{H}_2\text{O}) = \frac{6.0}{18.0} = 0.333 \text{ mol}$$

**Compare and conclude**

0.333 mol is larger than 0.25 mol, 0.247 mol and 0.136 mol. So 6.0 g of water contains the greatest number of moles, and therefore the greatest number of molecules.

options.A: 6.0 dm3 is only one quarter of the molar volume (24 dm3), so this is 0.25 mol of Ar atoms. This is a large amount, but it is less than the 0.33 mol in option D.
options.B: CO2 has a large Mr of 44.0, so 6.0 g is only 6.0/44.0 = 0.136 mol. This is the smallest number of moles here because a heavy molecule means fewer molecules per gram.
options.C: Mg has Ar of 24.3, so 6.0 g is 6.0/24.3 = 0.247 mol. This is very close to option A, but still less than the 0.333 mol of water.
options.D: Water has the smallest Mr of 18.0, so 6.0 g gives 6.0/18.0 = 0.333 mol, the largest moles of all four options. More moles means more molecules (moles x Avogadro constant), so this contains the greatest number of particles.
